<thought>We need to determine how many CH₃ groups are present in the unknown sample. The most direct way is to obtain the ¹H NMR spectrum, where each methyl group appears as a signal (typically a singlet, doublet, etc.) around 0.8–1.2 ppm. By counting distinct methyl resonances we can infer the number of CH₃ groups. Therefore, we will request the proton NMR spectrum for the sample.</thought>
